mainTopic: The new year of the אתרוג (שבט, by the calendar, even in a leap year), and how an אתרוג crossing into or out of שביעית is treated for מעשר and ביעור.
overview: The גמרא shows that רבה בר רב הונא's earlier statement cannot be right, because a ברייתא that follows רבן גמליאל's 'picking' rule still uses שבט. So his statement is corrected: even for רבן גמליאל, the אתרוג's new year is שבט. The גמרא then explains why the אתרוג ברייתא uses the example of the third year going into the fourth. An אתרוג tree handled by everyone in שביעית gives no fruit for three years. רבי ינאי teaches that the אתרוג's new year is the calendar month of שבט, and that it stays there even in a leap year. רבה and רב המנונא disagree about an אתרוג that crosses into or out of שביעית, and they treat מעשר and ביעור differently. A ברייתא of רבי שמעון challenges them both. The גמרא answers that the matter is a מחלוקת תנאים, and it brings the testimony of the five Elders and the vote at אושא. The amud ends by asking why the אושא ruling mentions שביעית at all, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבן גמליאל but says שבט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא about the אתרוג follows רבן גמליאל's 'picking' rule, yet it gives the date as שבט. That contradicts the version of רבה בר רב הונא which said תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the one we know holds that the אתרוג follows the time of picking? רבן גמליאל. And yet the ברייתא teaches שבט!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the earlier quote of רבה בר רב הונא. That quote said that for רבן גמליאל the אתרוג's new year is תשרי, but the ברייתא, which follows רבן גמליאל, says שבט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא judges the אתרוג by when it was picked, and that is רבן גמליאל's opinion. It also uses ט״ו בשבט as the cutoff date. So even according to רבן גמליאל, the new year must be שבט, not תשרי as the earlier version claimed.

keyTerms.meaning: Picking (harvesting) of the fruit
Whom have you heard who holds this? (a way of identifying whose opinion a source follows)
And yet it teaches
The month of שבט (ט״ו בשבט, the new year for trees)

phrases.aramaic: מַאן שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ דְּאָזֵיל בָּתַר לְקִיטָה —
phrases.english: Whom have you heard who goes after the picking?
phrases.notes: He means the opinion that an אתרוג is tithed by the year it was picked, the way vegetables are.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel. And yet it teaches Shevat!
phrases.notes: The ברייתא used the night before ט״ו בשבט as its cutoff date.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ דְּאָזֵיל בָּתַר לְקִיטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier quote of רבה בר רב הונא (from before this section) using the ברייתא about an אתרוג picked on the eve of ט״ו בשבט.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier version of רבה בר רב הונא: according to רבן גמליאל, the אתרוג's new year is תשרי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא follows the picking rule, which belongs to רבן גמליאל, yet it uses שבט as the cutoff. So according to רבן גמליאל the new year is שבט.

steps.title: רבה בר רב הונא's statement corrected to say שבט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords רבה בר רב הונא's statement. Even though רבן גמליאל treats the אתרוג like a vegetable for the picking rule, its new year is still שבט, like a tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if this was said, this is how it was said: רבה בר רב הונא said, 'Even though רבן גמליאל said an אתרוג follows picking like a vegetable, its new year is שבט.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the challenge by giving a corrected version of what רבה בר רב הונא said. The new year is שבט, not תשרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל borrows only one rule from vegetables: the אתרוג is judged by the time of picking. He does not move its new year to vegetables' date, so it keeps the trees' date of שבט. Now the ברייתא and רבה בר רב הונא agree.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, this is how it was said (a corrected version of a statement)
Even though
Like a vegetable
Its new year (for tithing purposes)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבן גמליאל, an אתרוג is judged by its picking time, like a vegetable, but its new year is still ט״ו בשבט, like a tree.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think that because the אתרוג follows picking 'like a vegetable' it also takes vegetables' new year of תשרי. The comparison covers only the picking rule, not the date.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said:
Rabba bar Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: Even though Rabban Gamliel said
an etrog follows the picking, like a vegetable,
its new year is Shevat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 by giving a corrected version of רבה בר רב הונא's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Corrected version of an Amora's statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For רבן גמליאל, the אתרוג's new year is תשרי, since he compares it to a vegetable.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבן גמליאל, the אתרוג follows picking like a vegetable, but its new year remains שבט.

steps.title: Why do the two ברייתות use different years as examples?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the vegetable ברייתא uses the example of the second year going into the third. The אתרוג ברייתא uses the third year going into the fourth instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different there, that it teaches 'if it was the second year going into the third,' and what is different here, that it teaches 'if it was the third year going into the fourth'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that two parallel ברייתות pick different years for their examples, and it asks why. This sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both examples show the switch between two kinds of tithes, מעשר שני and מעשר עני. The ברייתות could have used the same pair of years. Since they didn't, the גמרא suspects there is a reason behind the choice.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different there?
Here
The second year (of the שמיטה cycle) going into the third
The third year going into the fourth

phrases.english: What is different there, that it teaches
phrases.notes: 'There' is the ברייתא about someone who picked vegetables on the eve of ראש השנה.

phrases.english: 'If it was the second year going into the third'
and what is different here, that it teaches
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the ברייתא about the אתרוג picked on the eve of ט״ו בשבט.

phrases.english: 'If it was the third year going into the fourth'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new point about the wording of the ברייתות, separate from the שבט/תשרי question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the אתרוג ברייתא uses third-into-fourth instead of second-into-third like the vegetable ברייתא.

steps.title: The אתרוג tree is harmed by handling during שביעית
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is teaching a fact in passing. Handling harms an אתרוג tree. Since everyone handles it in שביעית, it does not bear fruit for three years, so the third year is the natural example.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us something in passing: handling harms an אתרוג. Since everyone handles it during שביעית, it does not bear fruit until three years later.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 3. The choice of the third year was deliberate, to teach a fact about how אתרוג trees grow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During שביעית the orchards are open to everyone, so many people touch the אתרוג trees, and this damages them. After that the trees take three years to bear fruit again. So the realistic case of picking אתרוגים is the third year, not the second.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter in passing (something taught along the way)
The hand (handling) is harmful to it
They handle / touch
The seventh year (שמיטה), when produce is open to everyone
Bears fruit

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא chose 'third going into fourth' on purpose. It teaches that an אתרוג tree handled by everyone in שביעית gives no fruit for three years.

phrases.aramaic: מִילְּתָא אַגַּב אוֹרְחֵיהּ קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן,
phrases.english: It teaches us a matter in passing:
that the hand is harmful to an etrog,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַיְּידֵי דִּמְמַשְׁמְשִׁי בֵּיהּ כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא בִּשְׁבִיעִית,
phrases.english: and since everyone handles it in the Sabbatical Year,

phrases.aramaic: לָא טָעֵין פֵּרֵי עַד תְּלָת שְׁנִין.
phrases.english: it does not bear fruit until three years.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִילְּתָא אַגַּב אוֹרְחֵיהּ קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא chose the third year to teach in passing that an אתרוג tree, handled by everyone in שביעית, gives no fruit for three years.

steps.title: When is the new year of an אתרוג?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks רבי ינאי on what date the אתרוג's new year falls.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן asked רבי ינאי: When is the new year for an אתרוג?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רבי יוחנן wants to know the exact date that starts a new year for an אתרוג. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The year an אתרוג belongs to matters for מעשר and שביעית. The question is simply which date marks the switch from one year to the next.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a request for information)
New year (here, the cutoff date for counting the fruit's year)
When?

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מֵרַבִּי יַנַּאי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan asked Rabbi Yannai:
An etrog, when is its new year?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מֵרַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new inquiry about the אתרוג's new year, building on the earlier discussion of whether it is שבט or תשרי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The date of the אתרוג's new year.

steps.title: The answer: שבט
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי answers that the אתרוג's new year is in שבט.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי answers that the אתרוג's new year is שבט, just like other trees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the conclusion of Step 2. The אתרוג follows the tree date of שבט, not תשרי.

keyTerms.meaning: The month of שבט, the new year for trees

phrases.english: He said to him: Shevat.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The new year of the אתרוג is in שבט.

steps.title: Which שבט: the calendar month or the solar season?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks whether 'שבט' means the month of שבט on the calendar or the 'שבט' of the solar seasons.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you mean שבט of the months, or שבט of the season?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן asks a follow-up to pin down what 'שבט' means. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Jewish calendar has months that follow the moon. It also has seasons, called תקופות, that follow the sun. A 'שבט' counted by the sun would fall on a different date each year, so he asks which one is meant.

keyTerms.meaning: Months (the calendar months, which follow the moon)
Season (counted by the sun)

phrases.english: Shevat of the months,
or Shevat of the season?
phrases.notes: He means the month-long stretch of the solar season that lines up with שבט, which shifts against the calendar each year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for more detail about the answer in Step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'שבט' means the month on the calendar or the solar season.

steps.title: The answer: the calendar month
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי answers that he means the month of שבט on the calendar.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Of the months.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי clarifies that he means the regular month of שבט on the Jewish calendar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cutoff date is fixed by the calendar month. It does not move around with the solar season.

phrases.english: He said to him: Of the months.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is the month of שבט on the calendar.

steps.title: What about a leap year?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן (some say רבי יוחנן asked רבי ינאי) what the rule is in a leap year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked רב נחמן, and some say רבי יוחנן asked רבי ינאי: If it was a leap year, what is the rule?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question: does the new year for trees change in a שנה מעוברת? This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A leap year adds a whole extra month, so the year is longer. The question is whether the trees' new year should shift later because of that extra month, or stay in שבט.

keyTerms.meaning: A leap year (a year with an extra month)
What is the rule?

phrases.english: Rava asked Rav Nachman,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מֵרַבִּי יַנַּאי:
phrases.english: and some say Rabbi Yochanan asked Rabbi Yannai:
If it was a leap year, what is the rule?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the date is a calendar month, it asks what happens when the calendar has an extra month.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the trees' new year shifts in a leap year.

steps.title: Follow most years
steps.stepSummary: The answer: go by the majority of years, so the new year stays in שבט.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Go after the majority of years.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is that a leap year does not change anything. Most years are regular, so we keep the same date of שבט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leap years are the minority. The rule is set by the normal year, so the new year for trees stays in שבט even when there is an extra month.

keyTerms.meaning: Go after the majority

steps.whatToRemember: The אתרוג's new year is the month of שבט on the calendar, and it stays in שבט even in a leap year.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַלֵּךְ אַחַר רוֹב שָׁנִים.
phrases.english: He said to him: Go after the majority of years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the leap-year question of Step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Follow regular years, so the new year stays in שבט.

steps.title: רבה's rule for an אתרוג crossing into or out of the שמיטה year
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules on two cases. An אתרוג from the sixth year that is picked in the seventh year is exempt from מעשר and from ביעור. An אתרוג from the seventh year that is picked in the eighth year is exempt from מעשר but obligated in ביעור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: An אתרוג of the sixth year that entered the seventh is exempt from tithes and exempt from removal. One of the seventh year that entered the eighth is exempt from tithes and obligated in removal.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives a new rule about an אתרוג that started growing in one year and was picked in the next year. One case crosses into שביעית and the other crosses out of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אתרוג can belong to one year by when it first formed, called חנטה, and to another year by when it was picked. In the first case, רבה is lenient on both counts: no מעשר and no ביעור. In the second case, it is exempt from מעשר but must have ביעור, the removal required for שביעית fruit.

keyTerms.meaning: A fruit from the sixth year (it began growing then)
The שמיטה year
Tithes
Removal: the מצוה to get rid of שביעית produce from the house once that kind of fruit is gone from the fields

phrases.english: Rabba said:
An etrog of the sixth year that entered into the seventh year —
phrases.notes: It started growing in the sixth year but was picked in שביעית.

phrases.english: is exempt from tithes
and is exempt from removal.
And one of the seventh year that entered into the eighth —
is exempt from tithes
and is obligated in removal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: אֶתְרוֹג בַּת שִׁשִּׁית שֶׁנִּכְנְסָה לִשְׁבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement applying the אתרוג's year rules to שביעית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sixth into seventh: exempt from מעשר and from ביעור. Seventh into eighth: exempt from מעשר and obligated in ביעור.
steps.confusionAlert: Remember that 'entered into' means it was picked in the later year. The fruit began growing (חנטה) in the earlier year.

steps.title: אביי: the first case seems to follow two different dates
steps.stepSummary: אביי accepts the second case because it is strict. But in the first case, being exempt from ביעור means we follow חנטה in the sixth year. If so, the אתרוג should be obligated in מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: It makes sense that the latter clause is strict. But the first clause, exempt from removal — why? Because we say to follow the time the fruit formed. If so, it should be obligated in tithes!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges the first half of רבה's rule. It seems to follow the forming date for one law and the picking date for the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exemption from ביעור makes sense only if the fruit counts as sixth-year fruit, by when it formed. But sixth-year fruit must have מעשר taken. So exempting it from מעשר too means treating it as seventh-year fruit, which contradicts the first point.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (I can accept this part)
The last part / the first part of a statement
To be strict
The stage when the fruit first forms
If so

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
It makes sense that the latter clause is to be strict,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא רֵישָׁא פְּטוּרָה מִן הַבִּיעוּר — אַמַּאי?
phrases.english: but the first clause, exempt from removal — why?
Because we say: go after the forming of the fruit,
if so, it should be obligated in tithes!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks the first half of רבה's rule in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling that a sixth-year אתרוג picked in שביעית is exempt from both מעשר and ביעור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The exemption from ביעור follows חנטה, which makes the fruit sixth-year fruit. Sixth-year fruit owes מעשר, so the exemption from מעשר seems inconsistent.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the question of whether one fruit can follow two different dates for two different laws. The answer will come next.

steps.title: רבה explains why the first אתרוג is exempt from tithes
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers אביי. In שביעית everyone is allowed to touch the fruit, so the אתרוג is treated as ownerless and is exempt from מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Everyone's hand touches it, and you are saying it should be obligated in מעשר?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers אביי's question about the first case. Even though we follow the sixth year for ביעור, this אתרוג is still exempt from מעשר for a separate reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי thought that following חנטה in the sixth year should also mean the fruit owes מעשר. רבה says the exemption from מעשר does not come from which year it belongs to. It comes from the fact that it was picked in שביעית, when everyone may enter and touch the fruit, so it counts as ownerless (הפקר), and ownerless produce is exempt from מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone's hand touches it, meaning the fruit is open to all
Tithes taken from produce
Ownerless property, which is exempt from מעשר

steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not saying the אתרוג belongs to the seventh year. He still follows the sixth year. The exemption from מעשר comes only because the fruit is ownerless at the time it is picked.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: יַד הַכֹּל מְמַשְׁמְשִׁין בָּהּ,
phrases.english: He said to him: Everyone's hand touches it,
phrases.notes: רבה is answering אביי. In the seventh year anyone may come in and handle the fruit.

phrases.english: and you say it should be obligated in tithes?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: יַד הַכֹּל מְמַשְׁמְשִׁין בָּהּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: A separate reason for the exemption: ownerlessness
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Following the sixth year for ביעור should also make the fruit obligated in מעשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fruit belongs to the sixth year, but it is exempt from מעשר because it is ownerless when picked in שביעית.

steps.title: רב המנונא says the אתרוג always follows the year it began growing
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא disagrees with רבה. A sixth-year אתרוג picked in the seventh year is always treated as sixth-year fruit. A seventh-year אתרוג picked in the eighth year is always treated as seventh-year fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said: A sixth-year אתרוג that enters the seventh year is always sixth-year fruit. A seventh-year אתרוג that enters the eighth year is always seventh-year fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא, רב המנונא, gives his own simple rule. The fruit always follows the year it began to grow, for every law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב המנונא, the first אתרוג is fully sixth-year fruit. That means it is obligated in מעשר and exempt from ביעור, and he does not use רבה's ownerless reason. The second אתרוג is fully seventh-year fruit, so it is obligated in ביעור and exempt from מעשר, just like רבה said.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit belonging to the sixth year, because it began growing then
Always, meaning for every law
The eighth year, the first year after שמיטה

phrases.english: And Rav Hamnuna said:
An etrog of the sixth year that enters the seventh year
phrases.notes: He means an אתרוג that began growing in the sixth year and was picked in the seventh.

phrases.english: is always sixth-year fruit,
and an etrog of the seventh year that enters the eighth year
is always seventh-year fruit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different opinion from רבה's rule in Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אתרוג always follows the year it began growing, for both מעשר and ביעור.

steps.title: A ברייתא says both אתרוגים are exempt from both tithes and elimination
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן יהודה in the name of רבי שמעון. Both kinds of אתרוג are exempt from מעשר and from ביעור, because each מצוה needs the fruit to grow and be picked in the obligated time.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא. רבי שמעון בן יהודה says in the name of רבי שמעון: A sixth-year אתרוג that enters the seventh year is exempt from מעשר and exempt from ביעור, because nothing owes מעשר unless it grew and was picked during a time of obligation. A seventh-year אתרוג that enters the eighth year is exempt from מעשר and exempt from ביעור, because nothing owes ביעור unless it grew in שביעית and was picked in שביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge the opinions we just heard. Here the ברייתא is only being quoted; the next step explains exactly whom it challenges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sets a strict test. A מצוה applies only if both the growing and the picking happened in a time when that מצוה applies. Since each אתרוג crossed a year boundary, it fails the test for both מעשר and ביעור.

keyTerms.meaning: Removing שביעית produce from one's house when it is no longer in the field
Grew during a time when the מצוה applies
Was picked

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
An etrog of the sixth year that enters the seventh year

phrases.aramaic: פְּטוּרָה מִן הַמַּעֲשֵׂר וּפְטוּרָה מִן הַבִּיעוּר,
phrases.english: is exempt from tithes and exempt from elimination,
because there is nothing that is obligated in tithes

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן גָּדַל בְּחִיּוּב וְנִלְקַט בְּחִיּוּב.
phrases.english: unless it grew during obligation and was picked during obligation.
phrases.notes: Here "obligation" means a year when מעשר applies, so not שביעית.

phrases.english: And an etrog of the seventh year that enters the eighth year

phrases.aramaic: פְּטוּרָה מִן הַמַּעֲשֵׂר וּפְטוּרָה מִן הַבִּיעוּר,
phrases.english: is exempt from tithes and exempt from elimination,
because there is nothing that is obligated in elimination

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן גָּדַל בִּשְׁבִיעִית וְנִלְקַט בִּשְׁבִיעִית.
phrases.english: unless it grew in the seventh year and was picked in the seventh year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא against רבה (Step 11) and רב המנונא (Step 14).
steps.kashyaTarget: The rulings of רבה and רב המנונא about an אתרוג that crosses a year boundary
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires both growing and picking in the obligated time, so it exempts both kinds of אתרוג from both מצוות.

steps.title: Pinpointing whom each half of the baraita challenges
steps.stepSummary: The first half of the ברייתא challenges רב המנונא. The second half challenges both רבה and רב המנונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first clause is difficult for רב המנונא. The last clause is difficult for both רבה and רב המנונא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly which opinions the ברייתא contradicts. It splits the problem by each half of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב המנונא says the sixth-year אתרוג owes מעשר, but the first half of the ברייתא exempts it. רבה avoids this problem because he also exempts it from מעשר. In the second case, both רבה and רב המנונא say the seventh-year אתרוג owes ביעור, but the ברייתא exempts it, so both are challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a teaching
The last clause of a teaching
It is difficult; a contradiction to someone's view

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רבה's ownerless reason protected him on the first case. The ביעור ruling in the second case is now under attack for both אמוראים.

phrases.english: The first clause is difficult for Rav Hamnuna,
phrases.notes: He said the sixth-year אתרוג owes מעשר, but the ברייתא exempts it.

phrases.aramaic: סֵיפָא קַשְׁיָא בֵּין לְרַבָּה בֵּין לְרַב הַמְנוּנָא!
phrases.english: the last clause is difficult for both Rabba and Rav Hamnuna!
phrases.notes: Both of them said the seventh-year אתרוג owes ביעור, and the ברייתא says it doesn't.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישָׁא קַשְׁיָא לְרַב הַמְנוּנָא, סֵיפָא קַשְׁיָא בֵּין לְרַבָּה בֵּין לְרַב הַמְנוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the exact targets of the ברייתא quoted in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב המנונא on מעשר in the first case; both רבה and רב המנונא on ביעור in the second case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא exempts the cases where these אמוראים ruled that the fruit is obligated.

steps.title: The issue is a dispute among the תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from the ברייתא by saying the issue is a מחלוקת תנאים. It brings a ברייתא with two views: the testimony of אבטולמוס about מעשר, and the vote in אושא about both מעשר and שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute among the תנאים. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי said that אבטולמוס testified in the name of five Elders that an אתרוג follows the time of its picking for מעשר. But our Rabbis voted in אושא and said it follows the time of its picking, both for מעשר and for שביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבה and רב המנונא. It says the ברייתא of רבי שמעון is only one opinion, and other תנאים hold differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is 'תנאי היא': the ברייתא from step 15 does not settle the question, because other תנאים disagree with it. In the new ברייתא, the five Elders made picking decide only for מעשר, which suggests a different rule for שביעית. The Sages at אושא then said picking decides for both מעשר and שביעית. Because the rule for an אתרוג was debated, an אמורא can follow a תנא other than רבי שמעון without being refuted.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute among the תנאים
A sage who passed on a tradition (testimony) from five Elders
Picking (harvesting) the fruit
They voted (they counted their opinions)
A town in the Galil where the Sages gathered and made rulings

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common way the גמרא answers a challenge from a ברייתא. An אמורא may follow another תנא who disagrees with that ברייתא.

phrases.english: It is a dispute among the Tannaim.
As it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yosei said:
Avtolemos testified in the name of five Elders:
An etrog follows the time of its picking for tithes,
and our Rabbis voted in Usha and said:
It follows the time of its picking,
both for tithes and for the Sabbatical Year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16 from the ברייתא of רבי שמעון against רבה and רב המנונא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a dispute among תנאים (תנאי היא): the challenging ברייתא is only one view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא of רבי שמעון seemed to disprove רבה and רב המנונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule for the אתרוג is a מחלוקת תנאים. The five Elders tied picking only to מעשר, and the Sages of אושא tied it to both מעשר and שביעית. So רבי שמעון's ברייתא is not binding on the אמוראים.

steps.title: Why does the ruling at אושא mention שביעית?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the wording of the ברייתא. The first statement only talked about מעשר, so why do the Sages in אושא add שביעית?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a gap in the ברייתא. The answer, which explains the wording, comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'both for מעשר and for שביעית' sound like they are adding something to an earlier view. But the testimony of the five Elders never mentioned שביעית at all. So it is unclear what the אושא ruling is adding to, and the ברייתא seems to be missing something.

keyTerms.meaning: Who mentioned its name? (Who said anything about it?)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a challenge to the halacha itself. The גמרא is only asking about the wording of the ברייתא, which mentions שביעית without any earlier lead-in.

phrases.english: Who mentioned anything about the Sabbatical Year?
phrases.notes: The five Elders only spoke about מעשר, so the word 'both' seems to come out of nowhere.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the ברייתא brought in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the אושא ruling speaks of שביעית as if it were adding to an earlier view, when the testimony of the five Elders mentioned only מעשר.
